title: Which Deposit Figure Is Measured in an Auto Loans Due Day Realignment
content:
Which figure is taken as the deposit measure, when the due day on a loan of the Auto Loans line is realigned, follows how long the borrower's Personal Checking account has been open, counted in whole months to the day of the realignment.

**Opened at least 120 whole months before the realignment:** the deposit measure is the largest recurring deposit ever posted to that account.

**Opened at least 48 but less than 120 whole months before the realignment:** the deposit measure is the total of the recurring deposits posted to it in the last three months.

**Opened less than 48 whole months before the realignment:** the deposit measure is the most recent recurring deposit posted to it.

## The three measures on one account

Take an active checking account in the Personal Checking line whose largest recurring deposit ever posted was 4100.00 USD, whose recurring deposits over the last three months total 7800.00 USD, and whose most recent recurring deposit was 2600.00 USD. Opened 130 whole months ago, the measure is 4100.00. Opened 60 whole months ago, it is 7800.00. Opened 20 whole months ago, it is 2600.00.

## The months at which the measure changes

An account opened exactly 120 whole months before the realignment takes the largest recurring deposit ever posted. An account opened exactly 48 whole months before takes the three-month total. An account opened 47 whole months before takes the most recent recurring deposit.

## Why a longer-held account is not always measured higher

The three measures are not versions of one number; they are different figures drawn from the same record of recurring deposits, and a longer-held account is not therefore measured on a larger figure. An account whose deposits have grown lately may read higher on the three-month total than on the largest single deposit ever posted.
